Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vheicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache
consistent with cervical whiplash injury. The mechanism of injury described is a plausible cause of the reported
symptoms. Over the course of care, the patient attended 21 visits, which is somewhat longer than typically expected
for this type of injury. Physical examination revealed limited cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle
tenderness, supporting the diagnosis, while neurological screening and imaging were within normal limits. Review of
prior records notes a minor cervical strain several years ago that resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing
records were reviewed and do not show duplicate or repeated charges for the same services. Treatment included
chiropractic adjustments, soft tissue therapy, and a home exercise program. At the time of the most recent visit, the
patient reported partial improvement, with ongoing intermittent stiffness and reduced tolerance for prolonged neck
positioning. Further follow-up is recommended to monitor progress and reassess functional status.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
